title: Incident chronology, evidence capture, and customer templates for model-serving degradations
author: Marina Holt
content:
Summary:

This playbook describes a repeatable, audit-ready approach to capturing incident chronology and forensic evidence for model-serving degradations (latency spikes, KV-cache regressions, token-level quality regressions, and sudden embedding anomalies). It also provides ready-to-send customer communication templates and status-page payloads appropriate for a range of severity levels. The goal is to reduce time-to-root-cause, ensure consistent customer communications, and preserve tamper-evident evidence artifacts for postmortem analysis and compliance.

Scope and intent:
- Affects: Redwood hosted and Dedicated inference endpoints, routing/proxy layer, and caching subsystems.
- Excludes: non-serving infra incidents (cloud provider console outages) except where they directly alter inference behavior.
- Intended audience: on-call engineers, bridge operators, SREs, and Customer Success for post-incident follow-up.

Quick reference (who does what):
- First Responder: acknowledge pager, assign incident id (INC-YYYY-NNN), start bridge.
- Bridge Lead: owns live remediation and customer-facing messages.
- Evidence Steward: ensures snapshots, logs, and artifacts are captured and stored in evidence-bucket with correct retention tags.
- Postmortem Lead: drives RCA, timeline, and action items.

Severity matrix and SLAs (table):
| Severity | Customer Impact | Time-to-Page | Bridge Target | Initial Customer Notice | SLO for Recovery |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| Sev 0 (Critical) | Global outage or >30% of requests failing | 5 min | 15 min | 30 min | Restore within 2 hours or escalate to execs |
| Sev 1 (High) | Significant latency increases or quality regressions for paid customers (>10% affected) | 10 min | 30 min | 60 min | Mitigate customer-visible impact within 4 hours |
| Sev 2 (Medium) | Partial degradation, single region or small customer set | 30 min | 1 hour | 4 hours | Recovery within 48 hours or temporary workaround |
| Sev 3 (Low) | Non-critical alert, non-customer affecting | On-call at discretion | N/A | N/A | Track as reliability ticket |

Detection and evidence checklist (first 30 minutes):
1) Acknowledge and classify severity. Assign INC- ID and create a title mapping to service and symptom (e.g., "INC-2026-042: kv-cache evictions -> elevated tail latency in us-west-2").
2) Start a bridge using our standard tooling (bridge.redwood.internal/new). Add the incident id to the bridge title.
3) Capture real-time signals and preserve them (Evidence Steward):
   - System metrics snapshot (Prometheus): export scrape for the incident window (t0-5m to t0+60m). CLI: `promtool snapshot --label=INC-2026-042 --from=$(date -u -d '5 min ago' +%s)`
   - Traces: export all traces for impacted services (trace-filter: service:inference* OR route:/v1/generate). Save as jaeger-<INC>.json.
   - Request/response samples: collect up to 250 request traces and model outputs (redact PII). Put them in evidence-bucket/inc-2026-042/requests/ with sha256 checksums.
   - KV-cache metrics: eviction rate, hit rate, capacity, cache-age histograms. Pull raw counters from /metrics and store as cache-metrics-<INC>.csv.
   - Router/proxy logs: capture 30 min of ingress/egress logs, include headers and response codes.
   - GPU/host telemetry: nvidia-smi logs, host dstat for the interval.
   - Configs: store current rollout config, model version, quantization flags, and feature flags active at t0.
4) Evidence metadata: each artifact must include: incident_id, collector_name, UTC timestamp range, checksum, and short description. Use filename pattern: <INC>-<artifact>-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>.

Triage and rapid containment (first 1–2 hours):
- If root cause appears to be model-quality regression, immediately route to fallback model (policy: fallback->reduced-params stable-1.2) and enable output sampling to measure regression impact. Document the switch in bridge notes.
- If root cause is noisy neighbor / GPU saturation: pin noisy job, scale up dedicated capacity (if reserved), or move selected customer traffic to regional fallback. Use the routing API: `redwoodctl routing reroute --from region=us-west-2 --to region=us-east-1 --percent=30 --inc INC-2026-042`.
- For KV-cache problems: disable cache warming jobs, increase cache capacity on read-only replicas, and perform cache-compact operation: `cachectl compact --target=pool-7 --inc=INC-2026-042`
- If evidence indicates a bad deploy/agent config change: roll back to previous service revision using `deployctl rollback --service inference-router --rev stable-2026-11 --inc INC-2026-042`.

Evidence preservation best practices (forensics-grade):
- Immutability: once an artifact is exported, set ACL/lock flag and record checksum. Evidence steward owns TTL and retention tags (default 90 days for incidents, 365 for customer-impacting).
- Redaction: PII must be redacted at source. Use `redact-requests --input=... --rules=pii-v2.json` before storing. Document redaction actions in bridge transcript.
- Chain of custody: append a short ledger entry to the incident record when adding or accessing artifacts: who, why, and checksum.

Customer notice templates (use as-is or adapt):
- Initial short (for status page / email-to-CSRs):
  Subject: [Redwood] Degraded model-serving performance (INC-2026-042)
  Body: We are investigating elevated latency affecting the inference API in us-west-2. Some requests may experience increased latency or errors. Our engineering team is actively investigating and we will post updates within 30 minutes. Impacted endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat.

- Initial expanded (for named customer with active SLA):
  Subject: [Action Required] Current inference degradation impacting your traffic (INC-2026-042)
  Body: Hi <CustomerName>, we’re reaching out to let you know we are investigating an issue affecting inference latency in us-west-2 that may impact requests routed to your dedicated pool. The current mitigation includes routing a portion of traffic to another region and enabling a fallback model. We will provide an update within 60 minutes and a follow-up once we identify root cause. Incident ID: INC-2026-042. If you need immediate assistance, reply to this message or contact your CS lead.

- Resolution (status page + direct):
  Subject: [Resolved] Inference performance restored (INC-2026-042)
  Body: The incident impacting inference latency in us-west-2 has been resolved. Root cause: a cache eviction storm triggered by an autoscaler misconfiguration. Mitigation: rolled back the autoscaler change and restored cache capacity; traffic has returned to normal for all affected customers. We’ve captured artifacts and will publish an RCA within 72 hours. Next steps: Postmortem scheduled; action items include safer autoscaler defaults and improved canary gating.

Status page payloads (JSON-ready text snippets):
- Sev 0 initial update: {"status":"investigating","impact":"High","summary":"Elevated errors and latency - engineering investigating","incident_id":"INC-2026-042","next_update":"2026-02-18T15:30:00Z"}
- Sev 1 cobbled update: {"status":"identifying_cause","impact":"Partial","summary":"Mitigation in progress: rerouting traffic and enabling fallback","incident_id":"INC-2026-042","next_update":"2026-02-18T16:00:00Z"}
- Resolved: {"status":"resolved","impact":"None","summary":"Service restored; RCA pending","incident_id":"INC-2026-042","postmortem_link":"/postmortems/INC-2026-042"}

Bridge operator checklist (short):
1. Create bridge and assign roles.
2. Run detection/evidence checklist and attach artifacts to the incident.
3. Post initial customer notice via status page and CS channel.
4. Trigger mitigation playbook most likely to remove customer impact.
5. When system is stable, capture post-mitigation evidence snapshot and update artifacts.
6. Close bridge only after at least 2 hours of stable metrics and customer confirmation for Sev 0/1.

On-call rotation tie-ins and handoffs:
- Handoffs must include: incident id, last action taken, evidence artifacts locations, and next monitoring check-in. Use the oncall-handoff template in the shift tool.
- Shadowing: new oncall engineers must complete two evidence-capture game days before handling Sev 1+ incidents.

Game day scenarios to validate this playbook (run quarterly):
- Scenario A: synthetic KV-cache eviction storm created by a canary that triggers autoscaler churn. Validation: team collects evidence, applies routing mitigation, and restores baseline within SLA.
- Scenario B: model rollout with silent output drift. Validation: evidence includes sample inputs/outputs; fallback to stable model executed and accuracy comparison logged.
- Scenario C: noisy neighbor GPU exhaustion. Validation: capture host telemetry, scale and re-route traffic, demonstrate chain-of-custody for artifacts.

Postmortem rubric and timeline:
- Postmortem must be opened for any Sev 0/1 incident within 24 hours of resolution.
- Deliverables (within 72 hours): timeline.csv (minute-granular events), list of artifacts with checksums, initial hypotheses, and immediate mitigations attempted.
- RCA draft due in 7 days, final postmortem in 14 days with assigned action items each owned and with a target due date.
- Postmortem structure: summary, timeline, impact (customers and internal), root cause analysis, contributing factors, detection lead time, mitigations, action items, and verification plan.

Retention and compliance notes:
- Default evidence retention: 90 days. Customer-impacting incidents: 365 days. Legal holds: notify Security/Legal to extend retention.
- Access control: only designated Evidence Stewards and Postmortem Leads can export immutable artifacts. Audit logs are required for every access.

Appendices:
A) Example minimal command snippets for evidence capture:
```
# Export Prometheus range
promtool snapshot --label=INC-2026-042 --from=$(date -u -d '5 min ago' +%s) --to=$(date -u +%s) --out=inc-2026-042-prom.json
# Export traces from Jaeger
jaeger-export --service-pattern=inference --start=$(date -u -d '5 min ago' +%s) --end=$(date -u +%s) --out=jaeger-inc-2026-042.json
# Upload and lock evidence
aws s3 cp ./evidence s3://evidence-bucket/inc-2026-042/ --recursive
aws s3api put-object-lock-configuration --bucket evidence-bucket --object-lock-configuration '...'
```

B) Example incident title taxonomy:
- INC-YYYY-NNN: <primary-symptom> — <location> — <primary-affected-service> (e.g., INC-2026-042: eviction-storm — us-west-2 — inference-router)

C) Escalation contacts (on-call and backup):

- Secondary: Priya Nair (pager)
